title: What is Overfitting and Underfitting?
description: Learn to recognize overfitting and underfitting, and master the key techniques for preventing both.
content:
**Overfitting** occurs when a model learns the training data too well, capturing noise and fluctuations rather than the underlying patterns. This leads to poor performance on unseen data and a failure to generalize. **High variance** is evidence of an excessively complex model.

To prevent overfitting, several techniques can be employed:
• Regularization methods like L1, L2, or Elastic Net add a penalty to the loss function to discourage overly complex models.
• Techniques such as K-fold cross-validation help ensure that the model performs well on various subsets of the data, offering a better estimate of its true generalization ability.
• In iterative learning methods (e.g., gradient descent), stop training once the validation error begins to increase, even if the training error is still decreasing (early stopping).
• Reducing the number of features or parameters decreases the risk of fitting the noise.
• Increasing the volume of training data can help the model learn more robust patterns instead of memorizing the available examples.

**Underfitting** occurs when the model is too simple and lacks the complexity or flexibility to capture and generalize patterns from the training dataset, resulting in poor performance on both training and validation data. **High bias** is evidence of an overly simplistic model.

To prevent underfitting, several techniques can be employed:
• Use a more complex model that can capture the subtleties in the dataset, such as moving from linear to polynomial regression or using a deeper decision tree.
• Introduce or construct new features that better represent the relationships within the data.
• Overzealous regularization can oversimplify the model, so tuning the regularization parameter appropriately is essential.
• In some cases, simply training the model longer can help it learn the necessary patterns if underfitting is due to insufficient training.

Quick reference:
• Overfitting -> high variance -> great on training data, poor on unseen data -> fix with regularization, cross-validation, early stopping, fewer features, or more data.
• Underfitting -> high bias -> poor performance on both training and validation data -> fix with a more complex model, better features, tuned regularization, or longer training.
